newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE PESO ENDS HIGHER ON INFLOWS.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE PESO ENDS HIGHER ON INFLOWS.

text.p: The Philippine peso edged up on Thursday on the back of corporate and export-related inflows, traders said.
It closed at 28.46 to a dollar from the previous 28.49. It stayed within a narrow range of 28.45/28.55 throughout the day. Volume was lighter at $58.5 million from $74.1 million.
"Banks were gradually selling their dollars. They don't want to sell it right away so the peso won't appreciate substantially," a trader said.
"And buyers were just waiting for banks with long dollar positions to sell," he added.
One trader said the market was waiting for more sales of dollars on Friday, which could strengthen the peso to 28.25.
He said he expected a corporate inflow of more than $100 million which had been rumoured to come in earlier in the week.
Traders said the central bank stayed away from the market but it quoted offer rates for the dollar at 28.70 and 28.80.
